We find the reciprocal of the base $({\color{blue}{2}}),$ and then raise that reciprocal to the same power but with the *opposite* sign $({{\color{red}{+3}}}),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{-3} & ={(\frac{1}{2})}^{3} \\  & =(\frac{1}{2})\times (\frac{1}{2})\times (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{1\times 1\times 1}{2\times 2\times 2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\end{aligned}
$$
